messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The induced schema Win <A4, B3, C2> represents a higher-order relation schema involving multiple arguments." -- cites: E5 (Figure 2): observation "The figure shows the induction of higher-order schemata from the tri-partite graph, and the induced schema Win <A4, B3, C2> is highlighted."
2. "The schema Win <A4, B3, C2> is represented as a set of (Actor, Rel, Actor) triples, where Actors are groups of noun phrases and Rel represents relations." -- cites: E2 (Section 4.1): quote "Event schemata are represented as a set of (Actor, Rel, Actor) triples in (Balasubramanian et al., 2013)."
3. "The induced schema Win <A4, B3, C2> is a 3-ary schema, as indicated by the figure." -- cites: E5 (Figure 2): observation "The figure shows that the induced schema Win <A4, B3, C2> is a 3-ary schema."
4. "The induced schema Win <A4, B3, C2> is part of the supplementary material provided by TFBA and (Chambers-13)." -- cites: E4 (Section 4.1): quote "schemata induced by TFBA and (Chambers-13) are provided as part of the supplementary material."

Cited evidence:
[E2] (text, Section 4.1, page 7): Event schema induction is deﬁned as the task of learning high-level representations of events, like a tournament, and their entity roles, like winningplayer etc, from unlabeled text. Even though the main focus of event schema induction is to induce the important roles of the events, as a side result most of the algorithms also provide schemata for the relations. In this section, we investigate the effectiveness of these schemata compared to the ones induced by TFBA. Event schemata are represented as a set of (Actor, Rel, Actor) triples in ( Balasubramanian et al. , 2013 ). Actors represent groups of noun phrases and Rel s represent relations. From this style of representation, however, the n-ary schemata for relations cannot be induced. Event schemata generated in ( Weber et al. , 2018 ) are similar to that in ( Balasubramanian et al. , 2013 ). Event schema induction algorithm proposed in ( Nguyen et al. , 2015 ) doesn’t induce schemata for relations, but rather induces the roles for the events. For this investigation we experiment with the following algorithm.
[E4] (text, Section 4.1, page 8): schemata induced by TFBA and (Chambers-13) are provided as part of the supplementary material.
[E5] (figure, Figure 2, page 4) (image attached): Figure 2: Overview of Step 2 of TFBA . Induction of higher-order schemata from the tri-partite graph formed from the columns of matrices A , B , and C . Triangles in this graph (solid) represent a 3-ary schema, n-ary schemata for n > 3 can be induced from the 3-ary schemata. Please refer to Section 3.2.2 for details. [image]

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E5 (Figure 2) states that the induced schema Win <A4, B3, C2> is highlighted and is part of the induction of higher-order schemata, which supports the claim that it represents a higher-order relation schema.

The evidence in E2 (Section 4.1) refers to event schemata being represented as (Actor, Rel, Actor) triples, not specifically the Win schema. The claim misattributes this representation to the Win schema.
The evidence in E5 (Figure 2) states that the figure shows the induced schema Win <A4, B3, C2> is a 3-ary schema, which supports the claim that it is a 3-ary schema.

The evidence in E4 (Section 4.1) mentions that schemata induced by TFBA and (Chambers-13) are provided as part of the supplementary material, but it does not specify that the Win schema is part of this material. The claim misattributes the supplementary material to the Win schema.
